## Slide 1

Kestrel Valley Youth Music — Ensemble Pathways Logic Model INPUTS A programme director, two teaching artists and a part-time administrator Rehearsal space at the community hall; a shared instrument store; a minibus on loan Part-time counsellor provided under contract (Avery R. Nolan Counselling Center) ACTIVITIES Partnerships confirmed with a memorandum of understanding and insurance documents. Attend orientation evenings and submit the programme description to school leadership Weekly after-school ensemble rehearsals at each partner site Curriculum levelled for each year group; reviewed annually OUTPUTS Avg. Ensemble rehearsals delivered per week across every participating partner site Termly concert programmes printed; recordings archived; photographs catalogued Ninety young people completing at least one full programme year SHORT-TERM OUTCOMES Increased musical skills, improved rehearsal attendance, and stronger goal-setting habits Young people report greater confidence performing in front of an audience LONG-TERM OUTCOMES Graduates continue in ensemble music beyond the programme year. Families report that music has become a settled part of household life Partner schools sustain an ensemble programme without external staffing
